title: Base Labs Releases Top Ranked Decision Model Mammoth-1 as Open Source
summary:
Elephant-1, a 9B parameter model, is the highest performing in its class and holds a lead on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index. It was launched alongside mammoth-1, a 27B parameter model that ranks #1 on the Jev Decision Index as the top decision model globally. Base Labs is open-sourcing the weights and training details for both, while Baseten is providing free access to the models via its Model APIs until Oct. 27.

The models used a 'swiss cheese' approach to validate and scale synthetic training data, where scaling data 16x contributed 20 index points and cleaning data added 8. Base Labs developers noted that the training proves recursive improvement is possible when an agentic LLM iterates on a simpler model, though recursive self-improvement still requires human oversight. The company anticipates further improvements over the coming weeks.

Today we’re releasing two decision models, elephant-1 (9B) and mammoth-1 (27B), trained by the @baselabs team, available for free for one week on our Model APIs.

mammoth-1 is #1 on the Jev Decision Index and elephant-1 is tied for #1 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index.

It’s a new model, but more importantly, this is an open-source model you can access, deploy, and post-train on Baseten (or wherever you do your best work).

The free week ends 10/27/26 at 11:59 PM PT. Try it and let us know what you think.

selectedTweets.text:
@baselabs have the best decision model in the world (Mammoth-1, 27b), and also the best under 15b (Elephant-1 9b, which also beats Jev!) The most exciting thing about this model work is that it crystallises something very clear about RSI: that recursive improvement is here with agentic workflows, but recursive self improvement isn’t here yet. Models are more than capable of iterating on a model that is either one rung down the capability ladder from itself, or one level simpler (ie an agentic LLM working on a decision model) but they are not capable of improving themselves yet. We’ve tried a lot to get LLMs to improve themselves (through building their own RL environments, training themselves, curating mid training data, etc) and it still relies on a heavy human hand in the loop. However, this decision model training was one of the first times where we set up this outer loop and it worked. Our decision model got better and better as we provided high level, meta-guidance to the agent and worked on the outer loop harness to install general principles for alternating the scaling of the data and subsequently correction of the data, both of which made the model better (20 aggregated index points for scaling the data 16x, 8 index points for fixing and cleaning the data!).

We’re offering this for free for a week on @baseten MAPIs, try it out and let us know what you think!

selectedTweets.text:
We trained the #1 decision models in the world, mammoth-1 and elephant-1! 

This is our first Base Labs model release and we're excited to open-source all weights and training details. We really focused on scaling high-quality data in these training runs – not only synthetically generating new decision data but stacking how we validated our data. This follows something called our 'swiss cheese' approach to looping over and improving training data.

There are also a bunch more low hanging fruit when it comes to training these models, and we expect that we'll improve quickly over the coming weeks.
